A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CodeV-R1 research, retitled QiMeng-CodeV-R1 in v3. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations in Tables 1–2, training and testbench measurements, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds benchmark-distribution, problem-type, code-length, and MAGE integration results.

M1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a limited inference adaptation: CodeV-R1 replaces MAGE's RTL-generation agent while other agents use Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The core automated verifier, round-trip synthesis, distillation, reward design, and adaptive DAPO algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The training corpora and VerilogEval/RTLLM benchmark coverage are retained. Appendix C.4 adds generation within a multi-agent environment using golden testbenches. The new table/graph analysis examines an existing benchmark subset rather than introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their comparator sets. New Table 10 adds a MAGE comparison involving Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Deepseek-R1-0528, DeepSeek-V3, and GPT-4o-240806 against CodeV-R1 with Claude support.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce embedding-centroid distance/similarity measurements, table/graph-subset accuracy, and code-length measurements excluding comments and blank lines. The MAGE experiment specifies replacing only the generation agent. Existing training budgets and main evaluation settings remain unchanged; the MAGE evaluation dataset and budget are not specified.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 substantially expands investigation of uneven benchmark gains through embedding distributions, problem-type performance, and code-complexity proxies. C.4 adds an agent-integration study. Existing curation ablations, scaling analyses, timing comparisons, error breakdowns, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 20 generated responses per query for pass@k estimation and the same descriptive prompt-length statistics. v3 adds no independent-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New substantive results include table/graph accuracy of 55.43% for CodeV-R1 versus 78.04% for DeepSeek-R1, embedding and code-length statistics, and MAGE pass@1 of 94.87% for CodeV-R1 with Claude versus 95.51% for Claude-3.5-Sonnet. Section 3.3.4 changes the verifier's false-negative rate from 2.7% to 0.3%, without explaining the revision's provenance. Main Tables 1–2 and retained appendix result tables are unchanged; the MAGE scores are not standalone performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly specifies that snippets and descriptions implementing the same function are treated as identical elements of F/L, refining the mathematical domain convention. Definition 2.1, Theorem 2.1, and the proof equations otherwise remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the DeepSeek-R1 outperformance claim explicitly to RTLLM, and the introduction removes the claim of being the first specialized Verilog reasoning LLM. The introductory false-negative reduction claim changes from 35.5% to 96.1%. The three central contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting benchmark gains to training-distribution alignment and weakness on table/graph problems, while qualifying what centroid similarity establishes. It also discusses agent-integration potential and attributes residual verification errors to simulation/randomization issues. The original limitations are retained in Appendix G.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a promised release into a reported release of model, code, and data, with a resource pointer. New analyses identify embedding/visualization tools and code-length preprocessing. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and prompts are retained; Table 3's added batch-size entry repeats information already in v1 Section 3.1.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for t-SNE, instruction-finetuned embeddings, and MAGE, and discusses differences from MAGE's verification and agent setup. It also removes the first-specialized-model novelty claim. The existing related-work coverage and principal positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title and front matter, edits methodological and results prose, separates pipeline stages more clearly, and supplies specific appendix cross-references. Appendix C is reorganized around added analyses, and the limitations move from Section 6 to Appendix G without substantive deletion.

P2.justification: The appendix gains a two-panel embedding-distribution figure and tables presenting centroid comparisons, table/graph accuracy, code lengths, and agent performance, substantially expanding its evidence displays. Existing displays are retained or renumbered. Tables 1–2 are regrouped and reformatted; Figure 2 swaps model colors while preserving all plotted values.

improvement.justification: v3 better explains uneven benchmark performance through the new Appendix C.1 diagnostics, adds evidence of agent integration, and narrows overbroad performance and novelty claims. These improve interpretation and transparency beyond v1's already substantial evaluation. The gains remain incremental: the new agent experiment lacks key evaluation details, and the changed false-negative rate is unexplained, limiting the strength of the additional evidence.
